The dialogue presents a 16-pack-year smoker (½ pack/day × 16 years) with a one-month history of nonproductive cough and dyspnea, *without* systemic symptoms (no fever, night sweats, weight loss, or hemoptysis in the past month), and *without* imaging or spirometric evidence of structural lung disease (normal CXR, HRCT showing no bronchiectasis, interstitial disease, air-trapping, or mosaic attenuation). **Clinical Summary:**  
A 40–50-year-old current smoker (16 pack-years, ½ pack/day) presents with a 1-month history of nonproductive cough and exertional dyspnea. [GAPS]

- Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) value (to quantify eosinophilic airway inflammation)

Adult-onset eosinophilic asthma
